Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The worst possible single operation cost corresponds to the vertex with the maximum out-degree in the directed graph, and the aggregate amortized cost is derived by dividing the total cost across all operations by the number of operations. In a directed graph with |V| vertices (assuming no self-loops), no vertex can have more than |V| − 1 outgoing edges, and the sum of all out-degrees across the graph equals |E| by definition.

* (a) The cost of the worst possible single operation is **|V| − 1**, which is achieved when one vertex has a directed edge to every other vertex in V, making its out-degree maximal.

* (b) The average amortized cost per operation via aggregate analysis is **|E| / |V|**, because the total cost over the sequence of |V| operations is the sum of the out-degrees of all vertices, which equals |E|, and dividing by the |V| operations gives the amortized bound.
